questions.prompt: Slot attention with identity projections, d=2, slots s1=(1,0), s2=(0,1), input x=(0,3). What attention weight does x give slot 1 after the softmax over slots? (3 decimals)
Slot-1 attention over four inputs is (0.2,0.2,0.4,0.2). After normalising over inputs, the third input's weight? (2 decimals)
If you remove the softmax over slots and normalise only over inputs, the most likely outcome is:
options: Training becomes deterministic, since the slot initialisation is no longer sampled.
Slots will each bind exactly one object, since inputs compete more strongly.
Several slots copy the same dominant object because nothing forces them to specialise.
The attention maps become uniform, because the normalisation removes all slot differences.

questions.prompt: A model gets mean IoU 0.15 with slot i vs object i, and 0.78 after Hungarian matching. What does this indicate?
options: The IoU is computed incorrectly in both cases, so neither number is usable.
The matching leaks labels into the predictions, so 0.78 is not a valid score.
The slots are good but ordered arbitrarily; the first evaluation was wrong.
The model is overfit to the training set, so the IoU drops in the first evaluation.
questions.explanation: Slots are unordered; optimal matching is the legitimate protocol.

questions.prompt: Matching cost matrix (rows objects, cols slots) [[0.2,0.9,0.8],[0.8,0.1,0.7],[0.9,0.6,0.3]]. Minimum total cost of an injective assignment? (2 decimals)
Squared Mahalanobis distance: variance 0.01 per axis, offsets 0.1 m in x and 0.2 m in y. (1 decimal)
A gate at chi-square 5.99 (2 dof) rejects a detection with squared Mahalanobis distance 7.4. What should the tracker do?
options: Double the covariance and retry in the same frame until the gate accepts it.
Treat the detection as a new object or clutter and let the track coast.
Delete the track immediately, because the object has clearly disappeared.
Assign it anyway because it is the nearest detection to the track.
questions.explanation: Gating prevents wrong assignments after long occlusions.

questions.prompt: A track moving at 0.2 m/frame was last seen at x=0.5 m; it is hidden for 5 frames. Predicted x at the first frame after the occlusion (6th frame after last sighting)?
Two identical objects cross; a position-only tracker swaps them. Which change fixes this most directly?
options: Match with a higher learning rate so that the identity updates faster.
Use more slots so that each object gets its own dedicated slot.
Predict each object's next position using its velocity before matching.
Increase the image resolution so the two objects look different enough.
questions.explanation: Identical appearance leaves motion as the identity cue.

questions.prompt: Find the flaw: a report says 'slots track objects' after showing high mask IoU on single frames. What does this miss?
options: Masks cannot have IoU.
Slots can only be evaluated on videos longer than a minute.
Identity consistency across frames and occlusion was never tested.
IoU should be computed on the background.
questions.explanation: Per-frame segmentation does not show persistent identity.

questions.prompt: Your slot model segments CLEVR-like scenes with 3-6 objects well but fails on scenes with 10 objects. Give two hypotheses and one test for each.
rubric: Hypothesis involving number of slots K versus object count, with a test varying K.
Hypothesis involving training distribution (never saw 10 objects), with a held-out count test.
Each hypothesis has a measurable prediction (e.g. FG-ARI vs object count).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would implement and evaluate data association with a gate for a track that is hidden for 8 frames, including what the covariance should do while hidden.
rubric: Predict with a motion model and grow the covariance each hidden frame.
Match with an optimal assignment on gated candidates only.
Report identity errors against a position-only baseline across occlusion lengths.
